This PR changes **9** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **34** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via GanttConfigSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **183** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `15a1d7bfd11719f68cf35a3c3d18b5a9a5271997` — the merge of head `60d2d1b8dc2443fe1f1fee27231476cda4377ca2` into base `f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 15a1d7bfd11719f68cf35a3c3d18b5a9a5271997 && git checkout 15a1d7bfd11719f68cf35a3c3d18b5a9a5271997
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba 60d2d1b8dc2443fe1f1fee27231476cda4377ca2 && git checkout -B drift-repro f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba && git merge --no-ff 60d2d1b8dc2443fe1f1fee27231476cda4377ca2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `371638f0c17753aaadc510f58bc24ac3cc191d0d`
Local-runs: none

PR #37427 (cards #36882 + #37385), ruling 7178358629 (option A, terms 1-6), dev report 7182745430. Read: both cards with every comment, the PR body, the 51-file net diff against `origin/main`, the head's 70 check-runs, the Test Core (10/10) job log, and source on `main` and the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run; `record-recognisers.mjs` was run as a reader only (`--template`, `--paths`). The dispatch and resume orders were not read, so every "per the resume order" statement in the dev report is unverified here.

M1 (must-fix) — this record is rendered at the wrong tier for this head and cannot be its record of record. The diff carries `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`; `reviewFace` on `origin/main` returns the schema face on one schema hit, whatever the hunk holds, and `--template --paths` over this PR's 51 paths prints `Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, `Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts + CITED-FILE` and a ④ section. The declaration face is the review owed by a `Clause-②: yes` line alone, and this PR declares `no`. Remedy: re-dispatch the review at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER on the next head, or move the two describe edits to their own PR. The judgments below stand as a TIER_DEFAULT reading only.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept sets and public surface, each change:
- `SelectOption.color` (`field.zod.ts`): untouched. No schema, export or authorable key moves; `check:api-surface` and `check:authorable-surface` ride green inside Lint & Repo Gates. Right.
- `getBadgeColorClasses`, `getSemanticColorName` (`@object-ui/fields`): signatures and return types kept, second parameter kept and unread; the three private symbols deleted were never exported. `getSemanticColorName` now answers `undefined` for every undeclared colour, where its docblock promised an answer for any non-empty value. That is a behaviour change on an exported helper, type-compatible, as ruled in term 1. Right.
- Dot branch: declared hex, else declared family, else gray. Right.
- Gantt `colorField`: rungs 1-2 kept, rung 3 and the status / state / priority / severity fallback removed, `getSemanticColorName` import dropped. A palette name stored as the value (`red`) now paints the default bar; `isColorLiteral` on `main` already defined rung 2 as hex / rgb / hsl, so this is term 2 as written. Right.
- Calendar: own hash and 8-stop palette deleted; hex and Tailwind-utility pass-through kept; a nine-family name now maps to that family's tint. Right on the declared side; see S2 for the undeclared side.
- Server: 50 colour declarations across 27 object files (counted off the diff). Mixed string / object arrays are safe: `selectWithOptions` maps each entry on its own, and the object form written reproduces the shorthand's label and value. Every declared colour equals the deleted table's entry for that value (pending yellow, failed / cancelled / canceled / rejected red, completed / active / approved / done green, in_progress / info blue, warning yellow, critical red, draft / none gray, archived indigo, delivered purple). Right.

Term 6: met, to the depth a static read reaches. The runtime walk the dev reports was not repeated. A grep at the head over `packages/**` (spec, cli, qa, lint, verify, tests excluded) for table values in option position without `color`, in object, shorthand and bare-line form, with the table's own normalisation (case, spaces and hyphens), finds none left. The other computed option lists (`MIGRATION_JOURNAL_KINDS`, `UNIT_DIMENSIONS`, `APPROVAL_ACTION_KINDS`, `APPROVAL_CANCEL_REASONS`, `UploadScopeSchema`) hold no table value. `sys_approval_request.status` is declared and pinned. Residue, none of it a miss under term 6: two settings-manifest options (`ai.manifest.ts` `none`, `auth.manifest.ts` `open`) are settings-form choices, not object selects; `http-delivery.status` and `sys_scim_connection_binding.decommission_status` are text fields; `examples/**` and the console preview samples turn neutral, which is the ruled reach. Not verified: any view that draws a badge for a field with no options.

Declared deviations:
- `view.zod.ts`, two `.describe()` strings: needed, because `main` publishes the retired derivation as the meaning of `colorField` ("hashed from the value", "a semantic color token derived from the value"). Text only. Two consequences: it puts the PR on the schema face (M1), and it shows the published meaning of an authorable key changes (M2). The calendar sentence is also not exact (S2).
- `record-color.ts` docblock: comment only, and correct against the code at the head. Accepted.

S1 (should-fix) — the changeset's "to keep a colour, declare it on the option: `color: 'green'`" does not keep the colour on Gantt bars. `createFieldColorResolver` returns a declared family name raw, and `GanttView` paints it as a CSS named colour (`blue` is #0000ff, `green` #008000), where rung 3 painted the palette hex (#3b82f6, #22c55e). The raw pass-through predates this PR, but this PR makes it the only path and routes authors, and the platform's own 50 declarations, through it. The calendar got a family map in this PR; the gantt did not. Map a rung-1 family name through `getSemanticHex` (still imported) with a pin, or file a card and correct the changeset sentence.

S2 (should-fix) — the calendar still colours an undeclared value when the value equals a family name. `ObjectCalendar` hands on `resolveColorFieldValue(colorRaw) ?? colorRaw`, and `resolveEventColor` cannot tell a declared option colour from a raw record value, so a record whose `colorField` value is `green`, with no option colour, paints green. The gantt paints the default for the same input, and the new calendar describe text says "a value that is no color is never turned into one". The PR body notes the declared half only. Either resolve families on the declared rung alone or say it in the describe and the changeset.

S3 (should-fix) — the first out-of-scope note needs a card and a changeset line. A declared colour outside the nine families and not hex (`teal`, `amber`) is accepted by `z.string()` and now renders neutral, with no warning anywhere: declared and not drawn. No platform or example option declares one (the twelve `amber` / `teal` hits at the head are object-level `color`), but a consumer app may, and the changeset's reach sentence covers only options with no `color`. The note has `carrier: none`.

Second out-of-scope note: outside the ruling, no card owed. App tiles, presence avatars and gallery cover seeds colour entities, not select options; chart series are excluded by name in the analysis the ruling executes (confidence gap c).

N1 (nit) — platform vocabularies are now half coloured (`failed` red beside neutral `success` / `succeeded`; `Active` green beside neutral `Revoked`). That is term 6 and the #37385 card as written (the table, not the hash); the #37385 acceptance clause "no platform badge turns neutral" reads wider than its own What section. A UX follow-up for the zone to weigh, not a contract defect.

N2 (nit) — `FAMILY_EVENT_COLORS.blue` is `DEFAULT_EVENT_COLOR`, so a declared blue and an undeclared event look the same on the calendar.

### ② Semver level

M2 (must-fix) — the head ships A (`Metadata-protocol: none`, every entry `patch`); B is the right reading. Grounds:
- AGENTS.md Post-Task 3: "a changed meaning or default is `semantic`", and a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves. An option with no `color` and a `colorField` with no option colours mean something else after this PR, in every app, and the PR edits the published spec text of `colorField` to say so.
- `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (ruling A on #25105): a changed meaning is invisible to the baselines, "so the declaration, not the diff, is still the carrier"; `none` beside `minor` is refused by design. The green `Check Changeset` shows only that `none` and `patch` agree with each other.
- Precedent on `main`: 24 pending changesets declare `semantic`, several for a changed default rendering of unchanged metadata (#35891, #35745, #35597), each with `minor`.
- Term 5's own words cannot both stand under #25105. Its `none` comes from the analysis line "No spec change", which failed (the spec text had to change); its `minor` comes from "the renderer's default changes for every app", which is the `semantic` kind. A drops the ruled `minor`; B drops only the label.

B is within the ruling's intent and needs no new maintainer decision: the zone amends the claim lines on both cards with an audit note citing #25105 and the failed premise (the ruling's premise clause calls a failed premise a fork to report, and the dev reported it). Keeping A is what would need the maintainer. To change: the PR body line, both changeset bodies, both claim lines; `@object-ui/fields`, `plugin-calendar`, `plugin-gantt` to `minor`. `@objectstack/spec` may stay `patch` (text only; the gate asks for one moved package at `minor`), as may the eight server entries.

Packages `l1-face` flags with no entry, each:
- `@object-ui/core`: one docblock in `record-color.ts`. No behaviour or type change. No entry owed.
- `@object-ui/plugin-grid`: two comment-only source edits and one test. Its rendering changes only through `@object-ui/fields`. No entry owed.
- `@object-ui/plugin-kanban`: two test files. None owed.
- `@object-ui/plugin-list`: one test file. None owed.
- `@object-ui/types`: one JSDoc on `KanbanCard.colorClass`. None owed.
All `@object-ui/*` sit in the one `fixed` group, so they version together anyway. N3 (nit) — patch entries for grid, kanban and list would put the neutral-badge note in the changelogs of the packages whose surfaces change; optional.

`Clause-②: no`: holds. No schema refuses a value it accepted, no export is removed, no signature narrows; every input accepted before is accepted now and draws differently. That is a changed meaning, not a narrowed or widened accept set, so no arm is owed and the `(narrowing)` face does not arise. The calendar newly recognising a family name is a behaviour gain on a string prop that already accepted any string.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags and `open_questions`:
- Open question, term 5 (A or B): answered in ②, B.
- Spec describe fence breach: content accepted; tier consequence is M1.
- `record-color.ts` docblock fence breach: accepted.
- Changesets `patch`, not the ruled `minor`: M2.
- `check:dev-prereqs` not measured: a local-state reading; no check-run on the head depends on it. Accepted.
- "CI red is unrelated": below.

Red check-runs, `Test Core (10/10)` and its roll-up `Test Core` (a required context). Signature confirmed in job 139685152551's log: one failure, `@objectstack/plugin-security` `src/insert-check-post-image.test.ts:580`, "[#16608] insert on driver-sqlite-wasm (:memory:) ... the scoping field lands IN scope", `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms`; 1 failed, 7311 passed; `Failed: @objectstack/plugin-security#test`.
- (a) Import closure disjoint from the diff: NO on a strict reading. The test boots `SecurityPlugin`, whose manifest registers `SysAudienceBindingSuggestion` (touched: one option gains `color: 'yellow'`); it imports `@objectstack/metadata-core`, whose index exports the touched `sys-metadata.object.ts`; and three `@objectstack/spec` subpaths. The intersecting hunks are option `color` literals only, which no insert or RLS path reads.
- (b) Same shard green on `main` recently: yes. `Test Core (10/10)` is `success` on the six newest `main` commits that ran it (f9dd0331, ee11fce9, a0b01fab, ecbe854b, 5078f2ff, 15e80d2a). That plugin-security ran in shard 10 on each was not checked.
- (c) First error a timeout, not an assertion: yes. It is the first test of the sqlite-wasm arm; the file took 12.9 s for 25 tests and the package reports 1214 s of cumulative import time, which reads as runner load.
Judgment: very probably unrelated, but it does not qualify on the three facts, because (a) fails as stated. The red conclusion stands as this head's gate verdict. M2 forces a new head, whose run governs; the same signature again is a stop-and-diagnose, and no anchor card for it was found.

`Fixes #37385`: consistent with the cards. Term 6 says "landed before or with the ui PR"; #37385's body, triage comment and claim all say it is carried in this PR; its acceptance (every enumerated option declared, the PR lists them) is met; `PR-body guards` is green. Closing it on merge is intended. Whether the resume order asked for `Fixes` over `Refs` was not read. #36882's Skills-docs line is carried by #37406, open.

SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): the diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join; it is renderer logic, option literals, describe text and tests. Nothing to flag.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-36882-select-colour-iff-declared`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `371638f0c17753aaadc510f58bc24ac3cc191d0d`
**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5: contract record 7182916794 reads FAIL. The declaration is wrong (M2), three behaviour gaps are owed, and the next head is reviewed on the schema face at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (M1).

1. **Shape**: open draft against `main`, 51 files (+549/−326), `Fixes #36882`, `Fixes #37385` (intended: term 6 and #37385's own claim carry it here), `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. `l1-face` flags:
   - `changeset` on core, types, kanban, list and grid. Not owed: docblock, test or comment only.
   - `all-checks`: one red, see 3.
2. **Premise**: term 6 is met to a static read. 50 colours on 27 files equal the deleted table's entries, and `sys_approval_request.status` is declared and pinned. `Clause-②: no` holds: nothing is refused or narrowed, only drawn differently. No SQL push-down finding.
3. **Owed in this PR**:
   - **M1.** The diff touches `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`, so the review face is schema and the tier is `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. The seat's brief named the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT`; that is the seat's error, not the dev's. The delta is reviewed on the schema face at tier. Keeping the two describe edits here is fine.
   - **M2.** Ship B: `Metadata-protocol: semantic`, with `@object-ui/fields`, `plugin-calendar` and `plugin-gantt` at `minor`. An omitted `color` now means neutral, which is a changed default, and AGENTS.md makes that `semantic` (at least `minor`). Term 5's `none` rested on "No spec change", which failed, so B is within the ruling (#25105 ruling A). Amend the claim lines with an audit note citing that. `@objectstack/spec` and the server entries may stay `patch`.
   - **S1.** On Gantt, a declared family name (`color: 'blue'`) paints as a CSS named colour (#0000ff), where before it painted the palette hex. The PR makes that raw path the only one. Map it through `getSemanticHex` with a pin, or file a card and correct the changeset sentence.
   - **S2.** The calendar still colours an undeclared value that happens to equal a family name (`resolveEventColor` can't tell a declared option colour from a raw value), which contradicts the new describe text and the gantt. Fix it, or file a card and soften the text.
   - **S3.** A declared colour outside the nine families (`teal`, `amber`) passes the schema and now renders neutral with no warning. File a card (the note says `carrier: none`) and add a line to the changeset's reach.
   - **Red.** The `Test Core (10/10)` timeout (`plugin-security` `insert-check-post-image.test.ts:580`) does not meet the three facts, because the import closure intersects the diff on option-colour literals only. It stands as this head's verdict. The rework push merges main. If the same signature appears again, stop and diagnose rather than re-run.
4. **Accepted deviations**: the two describe-only `view.zod.ts` edits (docs consequence of term 2) and the `record-color.ts` docblock. Nits N1 (half-coloured platform vocabularies, as term 6 is written; a UX follow-up for the zone to weigh), N2 (declared blue looks like the default event tint on the calendar) and N3 (optional patch entries for grid, kanban and list).
5. **Out of scope and where it went**: value-hash colours on app tiles, presence avatars, gallery covers and chart series are outside the ruling, and no card is owed. Out-of-family colours go to the S3 card.
6. **Landing terms**: ungoverned, schema face at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Owed: a same-head at-tier PASS with M1, M2 and S1–S3 closed, green checks, and an **ACCEPT**. The area lands it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9fc4e9b3de7c50a9803b231e5fedb57e9d73d4b1`
Local-runs: none
